name: Canyon Gathering System (Kaskida gas export line)

values.OtherEnglishNames: Canyon Gas; Kaskida gas export line
values.EndLocation: Tie-in to Magnolia Gas Gathering Pipeline

researcher_notes: Enbridge press release of 3 October 2024 says it sanctioned and will build, own and operate the Canyon Gathering System, a 12 inch, 125 million cubic feet per day gas line for the bp Kaskida field. It connects subsea to Enbridge's existing Magnolia Gas Gathering Pipeline, which feeds Garden Banks Gas Pipeline. Expected in service by 2029. Offshore Magazine, reporting Enbridge, gives about 60 miles of pipe, starting at Keathley Canyon Block 293 in about 5,900 feet of water, growing to about 115 miles if bp exercises its options. The 195 km in the consolidator note does not match: 60 miles is about 97 km, and 195 km is close to the 115 mile option case or the oil line, so the 60 mile figure is staged. Cost of about 700 million US dollars covers the oil and gas lines together, so no cost is staged. This is a gathering line, and PipelineType gathering is in the GEM vocabulary. It is not the Magnolia Intrastate Pipeline (P0294, Louisiana onshore) or P2559 Magnolia Gas Pipeline, which are different systems. No existing row found for Canyon. Both sources trace to the same Enbridge announcement, so not independent; tier medium. Status proposed because construction has not started, with FID reached. No public route found, so route is unavailable. Exact end tie-in location not stated.
